description: Inventory a set of supplied cloud log exports (a directory, or files named one by one; JSON, JSON Lines, CSV and gzip of those) without parsing their records into rows: per file the format, the provider and the tenant, project or account its records name (identifiers only), the record count, how many records a reader of this pack takes (cloud_normalise's adapters, cloudtrail_parse, ual_parse, signin_analyse) and how many none takes, the time range the records carry, the markers of a next page (nextPageToken, NextToken, nextLink, @odata.nextLink) and whether the count equals a result cap (5,000 or 50,000, or the result_size the caller recorded). For the set: the interval requested in a small acquisition.json the caller writes (who exported, the query, the permission, the interval) against the interval returned, duplicates within and across files, gaps of a day or more between the files' time ranges, and pages named page-K-of-N that are missing. Export completeness is stated apart from logging and retention completeness, which this recipe does not assess. A receipt (coverage.json, with index.tsv, files.tsv and findings.tsv) exists from the first moment and is rewritten after every step; each input has its own status; an earlier run's receipt is never overwritten; a stop signal leaves the partial receipt and one line of JSON. The recipe starts no program and prints no record value. A stop that arrives before the script's first line has run (the interpreter's own start) gets no answer.
covers: Per file: format, provider, tenant or project or account, record counts (counted, taken by a reader of this pack, taken by none, rejected), the time range, next-page markers and result-cap matches; for the set: the interval requested against the interval returned, duplicates, gaps between ranges and missing named pages. Export completeness only: coverage.json says apart that logging and retention completeness are not assessed. It leaves out: what the provider logged, how long it kept it, audit configuration and delivery delay (an export says what was exported, and nothing here is a statement about logging or retention); record values (a record is classified by the fields it carries and counted, not parsed into rows: cloud_normalise does that); archives (.zip, tar and the like), which are named and not opened; and a record larger than 16 MiB or malformed, which is counted as rejected and not classified. A gap, a cap match, a next-page marker or a missing page is a reason to doubt that the export is whole; the absence of all of them does not show that it is. files.tsv and findings.tsv hold file names and tenant, project and account identifiers and are marked secret-bearing in the receipt (the mark is informational: nothing in the harness reads it for a decision); the directory is private (0700, files 0600).
